body:
## Summary

Same defect class as `a707c193c`'s fix for `FdBlackScholesVanillaEngine` ("Keep finite-difference American prices at the exercise value"): the step condition enforces the exercise constraint on grid nodes, but the monotonic cubic interpolant used to read off the price at the spot (which generally falls between nodes) can still undershoot the payoff there. `VanillaOption::impliedVolatility` prices Americans with this engine, so a value below the payoff cannot be inverted either.

`FdHestonVanillaEngine` never received the equivalent fix.

## Verification

Confirmed by a parameter sweep at the engine's own default grid (`tGrid=100, xGrid=100, vGrid=50`) across spot/strike/vol/maturity/rate/dividend combinations, using a near-BS-degenerate Heston process (tiny vol-of-vol, `theta == v0`) to isolate the finite-difference behavior from any genuine stochastic-volatility effect: **144 of 3696 combinations priced below intrinsic**, worst found ≈7.3e-3 (a 1095-day in-the-money call). Re-ran the identical sweep against the fix: **0 undershoots**.

## Fix

Mirrors the existing fix exactly: same exercisability switch (American/Bermudan/European, with the `payoffAtExpiry` carve-out), same "greeks stay on the interpolant" rationale (resetting them would disagree with a bump wherever the undershoot is local). Additionally floors the engine's own multiple-strikes caching path (`enableMultipleStrikesCaching`), which `FdBlackScholesVanillaEngine` has no equivalent of — leaving it unguarded would have left an inconsistency between the cached and uncached pricing paths for the same option.

## Test

Added `testFdHestonAmericanNotBelowExerciseValue` to `test-suite/fdheston.cpp`: two of the sweep's confirmed undershoot cases, plus negative checks (a European option and a not-yet-exercisable American must *not* be floored) adapted to the same near-degenerate Heston setup, asserting strictly-below-intrinsic rather than an arbitrary absolute gap. Confirmed it fails against the pre-fix engine and passes against the fix. Full `FdHestonTests`, `HestonModelTests`, `EuropeanOptionTests`, and `HybridHestonHullWhiteProcessTests` suites pass with no regressions.

🤖 Co-worked with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

review_comments.body: The multiple-strike cache lookup compares exercise type and dates but omits `payoffAtExpiry()`, which now controls whether the value is floored. Americans with identical dates and strikes but different payout flags can therefore reuse an unfloored undershoot or an incorrectly floored value, depending on pricing order. Include the payout flag in the cache comparison and add a regression covering both request orders.

Good catch, fixed in dcc42e8cf — added a payoffAtExpiryOf() helper (false for European, which has no payoffAtExpiry() of its own) and included it in the cache-lookup comparison alongside exercise type and dates. Added a regression test covering both pricing orders (two Americans sharing a cached strike, one with payoffAtExpiry=false and one true), confirmed it fails against the pre-fix cache key and passes with the fix.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

title: Keep `FdHestonVanillaEngine` American prices at the exercise value
